key_insight: Privileged training teachers help an Alzheimer's classification model learn from varied imputations of missing tests and produce confidence estimates that reflect missing information.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support research toward more reliable predictions when patients have incomplete clinical, biospecimen, or imaging data.
method: Generate multiple candidate fills for missing modalities, one modality at a time.
During training, use a diagnosis-informed teacher to grade fills and a full-data teacher to supply soft diagnostic targets.
At inference, predict from a single imputation rollout without privileged teacher information.
evidence_signal: On ADNI, the method outperformed state-of-the-art baselines; on two external cohorts, discrimination remained competitive and calibration error matched the lowest after all methods were recalibrated.
watch_item: The abstract does not report cohort sizes or effect sizes, and prospective validation is needed before clinical use.
paper_title: Privileged On-Policy Distillation for Calibrated Alzheimer's Diagnosis With Missing Modalities
